events.summary: China said it would expand training opportunities for Sri Lankan participants.
President announced plans to digitise the country within three years.
President said digital identity card work would be completed within eighteen months.
Sri Lanka introduced its first National Social Protection Policy.
First irrigation water released for Mannar’s 2024–25 Maha cultivation season.
Colombo–Jaffna train services resumed after track rehabilitation.
Postal Department began delivering voter cards for the 2024 general election.
Colombo–Kankesanthurai rail service was scheduled to resume on October 28.
Government appointed three teams to monitor foreign intelligence reports around the clock.
Transport minister instructed officials to issue free travel passes to railway employees.
Election Commission handed official voter cards to the postal department for distribution.
Eastern Province governor directed local councils to improve revenue and waste management.
CEB submitted a further electricity tariff reduction proposal to the utilities commission.
Australia provided a Beechcraft King Air 350 surveillance aircraft to Sri Lanka Air Force.
Health officials and police carried out dengue inspections and control measures in Batticaloa.
Police Hospital plans to hand over the renovated patient ward for police inspectors’ use.
Police and intelligence agencies are implementing a special security plan for foreign tourists.
Sri Lanka plans to seek membership in the BRICS-established New Development Bank.
WFP launched the five-year climate adaptation programme for farming communities in India and Sri Lanka.
China handed Sri Lanka a grant for relief to people affected by recent floods.
Cabinet approved phased development of the East Container Terminal as a fully owned terminal.
Civil works contract for the terminal has been awarded.
Cabinet approved declaring the East Container Terminal a special project.
Hospital staff are cultivating vegetables to support patients’ mental wellbeing.
A new version of Sri Lankan passports entered use.
India doubled its grant allocation for upgrading nine plantation-sector schools.
Cabinet approved passport procurement to maintain uninterrupted issuance.
President said the next budget would consider increasing public employees’ salaries.
President said the February budget would consider increasing public employees’ salaries.
Railway Department said Yal Devi services would resume on October 21.
Colombo–Batticaloa train service returned to normal operations.
Minister instructed departments to connect Western Province permits with other provinces.
Renovated sports complex with indoor arena and swimming pool opened in Omandai.
Rehabilitation of the Iranamadu left bank water supply canal is underway.
Pakistan High Commission distributed food to flood-affected families.
SLBFE launched a programme for migrant workers to submit complaints.
Government announced four bodyguards for ministers, with changes for security threats.
President ordered immediate flood relief and property reconstruction, with further funding if needed.
Navy deployed eight flood relief teams to assist affected residents across three districts.
President directed allocation of Rs 50 million for immediate flood and landslide relief.
Government plans SMS alerts for national security emergencies and human trafficking information.
President directed allocation of Rs. 50 million for disaster relief services.
The temporarily closed Welipanna interchange on the Southern Expressway reopened.
WFP representatives agreed to continue ongoing programmes in Sri Lanka.
Police introduced hotline 1997 for reporting misuse or theft of government vehicles and property.
Special transport and security arrangements were implemented at district secretariats for election nominations.
The Maho-Anuradhapura railway section was built at a reported cost of 30 billion rupees.
Railway officials took over the delayed section and directed trains to run slowly while unfinished repairs continue.
The railway section was scheduled to open on October 22.
Welipanna Interchange on the Southern Expressway was temporarily closed due to flooding.
The President directed officials to provide sugar factory land to farmers for short-term cultivation.
A breast cancer awareness rally was held in Kaluvaanchikudy with local health services support.
A district dengue-control inspection campaign was planned for October 13 to 15.
Governor directed agencies to intensify measures to curb AIDS in Eastern Province.
Cabinet ended pre-September 30 contracts for the agriculture modernisation programme.
Sri Lanka signed the World Bank RESET development policy financing second tranche agreement.
India offered assistance to modernise Kankesanthurai Port.
India decided to gift 22 diesel locomotives to Sri Lanka Railways.
The Finance Ministry said approval was obtained to restructure sovereign bonds.
A road near Temple Trees opened to public traffic.
Korea Exim Bank said it would resume concessional financing for Sri Lankan development projects.
Officials are providing free birth certificates to children without them nationwide during October.
Government departments planned a nationwide birth certificate programme for children lacking certificates.
Government decided to provide paddy farmers a fertilizer subsidy of LKR 25,000 per hectare.
China pledged full support for Sri Lanka's debt restructuring and economic stability.
IMF and government reviewed the programme and discussed the fourth tranche.
Election Commission halted the increased fertilizer subsidy of Rs 25,000 per hectare.
Agriculture Ministry planned to release Maha season irrigation water from October 15.
Officials discussed starting the second phase of Bandaranaike Airport development soon.
Officials discussed starting digital television broadcasting soon.
Fifteen government vehicles were returned to their respective agencies.
Officials discussed starting the airport development project's second phase soon.
Officials discussed starting Rupavahini digital broadcasting soon.
SLTB resumed bus service from Keerimalai to Colombo.
The President instructed officials to pause Grade Five Scholarship paper marking for two weeks.
